title: The Place In Which, The Law With Which

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *el que* and a preposition from B1 Unit 20: the preposition goes before *el que*, *la que*, *los que* or *las que*, and the article matches the noun (*el edificio en el que vivimos*). They are the tool for describing institutions: the place in which a community decides, the law with which a country recognises its patrols.

items.spanish: La asamblea es el lugar en el que la comunidad discute los casos.
items.english: The assembly is the place in which the community discusses cases.

items.spanish: La Constitución de 1991 reconoce a las comunidades indígenas, a las que permite aplicar su propia justicia en su territorio.
items.english: The 1991 Constitution recognises the indigenous communities, which it allows to apply their own justice in their territory.

items.spanish: Las rondas campesinas son organizaciones de las que forman parte muchos campesinos.
items.english: The peasant patrols are organisations that many peasants belong to.

items.spanish: La ley de 2003 es la norma con la que Perú reconoció a las rondas.
items.english: The 2003 law is the rule with which Peru recognised the patrols.

sections.content: Keep the preposition that the verb or noun needs, and match the article: *la ley con la que*, *los vecinos con los que*. Without the preposition the sentence is wrong: not *el lugar que la comunidad discute los casos*.
